title: How does an ECDIS safety contour work?

scenes.label: KNOW YOUR EQUIPMENT
scenes.heading: One ECDIS setting separates safe water from danger.
scenes.narration: One setting on your ECDIS decides where safe water ends. Set it wrong, and the grounding alarm may warn you too late.

scenes.label: WHAT IS IT?
scenes.heading: The safety contour
scenes.body: A depth contour you select. ECDIS draws it as a bold line between safe and unsafe water, and alarms before you cross it.
scenes.narration: The safety contour is a depth contour you select. ECDIS shows deeper water as safe, shallower water as unsafe, and alarms before you cross the line.

scenes.label: HOW IT WORKS
scenes.heading: ECDIS picks the next deeper contour
scenes.narration: Here is the catch. If you enter twelve metres and the chart has no twelve metre contour, ECDIS uses the next deeper one available. Here, that is fifteen metres.

scenes.label: SETTING IT
scenes.heading: What goes into the value
scenes.narration: To set it, start with your deepest draught. Add squat at your planned speed, and the under keel clearance your company requires. Allow for height of tide only where your procedures permit it.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: The alarm only protects you if the contour is right.
scenes.narration: Check it in every passage plan. The alarm only protects you if the contour is right.

meta.description: The ECDIS safety contour marks the boundary between safe and unsafe water and drives the anti-grounding alarm. See how ECDIS chooses the contour, what goes into the value and the most common mistake officers make.
